title: Lena Maris
biography_text:
Lena Maris (born 14 March 1985) is a community-based Social Worker known for her work with youth and families in the coastal city of Harborside. She has focused on school-linked services, neighborhood resource centers, and prevention programs for young people. Over her career, she has worked for public agencies and nonprofit organizations, while maintaining her primary role as a Social Worker in direct practice.

Early life and education

Maris was born in Harborside, a medium-sized port city with mixed residential and industrial areas. She grew up in the North Wharf district, an area with varied income levels and a wide range of cultural backgrounds. Her parents worked in hourly-wage jobs, and her family moved several times within the city. As a student, she attended North Wharf Primary School and later Harborside Central Secondary School.

During secondary school, Maris volunteered in a peer tutoring program and a student-run food drive. These activities led her to explore community service as a possible career path. She later enrolled at Harborside City College, where she completed an associate degree in human services. Afterward, she transferred to the regional State University at Harborside, earning a Bachelor of Social Work (BSW) degree. She continued her studies and obtained a Master of Social Work (MSW) with a concentration in community practice.

Early career

Following graduation, Maris accepted a position as a Social Worker with the Harborside Department of Youth and Family Services. In this role, she conducted home visits, coordinated with school staff, and helped families access housing, health care, and childcare resources. Her caseload included children with frequent school absences, youth facing family conflict, and newly arrived immigrant families adjusting to the local school system.

Maris participated in the department’s pilot program for integrated case management. The program aimed to reduce the number of separate assessments families had to complete. As a Social Worker in the program, she helped design a shared intake form and collaborated with school counselors, public health nurses, and housing advocates. She also received training in basic conflict resolution and trauma-informed practice, which she applied during home visits and school meetings.

Community-based practice

After five years with the city department, Maris joined the nonprofit Harborside Neighborhood Resource Network as a Social Worker. The organization operated drop-in centers in several districts, including North Wharf. At the North Wharf center, Maris organized walk-in hours for youth and families, led small psychoeducational groups, and provided one-on-one support.

Her work included helping youth navigate school transitions, such as moving from primary to secondary school or planning for postsecondary training. She also supported parents in understanding school policies, special education processes, and local transportation options. In addition, she coordinated with local libraries and community centers to host information sessions on topics such as digital safety, job search skills, and access to public benefits.

School-linked initiatives

Maris later accepted a school-linked Social Worker position shared between two secondary schools, Harborview Secondary and North Wharf Technical Academy. In this role, she divided her time between the two campuses. Her responsibilities included meeting with students referred for social or emotional concerns, conducting basic needs assessments, and connecting families to community resources.

She developed a referral pathway that allowed teachers, coaches, and administrative staff to contact her through a secure online form. Maris then scheduled follow-up meetings with students and, when appropriate, with their caregivers. She also coordinated with local mental health clinics to arrange further evaluation for students who needed specialized services.

Program development and supervision

Over time, Maris took on additional responsibilities in program design and supervision, while remaining a practicing Social Worker. She served as lead Social Worker for a multi-year youth engagement project funded by a regional foundation. The project focused on improving attendance and reducing school exclusion through mentoring, small group activities, and family outreach.

As lead Social Worker, Maris helped create simple screening tools to identify students who might benefit from early support. She supervised a small team of junior Social Workers and graduate-level social work interns, providing guidance on documentation, confidentiality, and interagency communication. She also coordinated regular case review meetings with school administrators and community partners.

Professional interests and methods

Maris’s work as a Social Worker emphasizes accessible services, early intervention, and collaboration. She commonly uses strengths-based assessment, solution-focused brief interventions, and structured goal-setting with students and families. She has integrated basic motivational interviewing techniques into her practice when discussing school attendance, substance use risk, or future planning with youth.

In addition to direct practice, Maris contributes to internal training sessions for new Social Workers at her organization. She has developed orientation materials on topics such as mandated reporting requirements, safety planning for home visits, and respectful communication with families from different cultural backgrounds. She has also participated in local interagency committees on youth services, representing the perspective of school-linked Social Workers.

Later activities

Maris continues to work as a Social Worker in Harborside, combining school-based duties with community outreach. She maintains a part-time schedule at Harborview Secondary while spending the rest of her workweek at the North Wharf neighborhood center. Her ongoing projects include helping to update the center’s resource directory, piloting a text-message reminder system for appointments, and supporting a youth advisory council that provides feedback on services.

Throughout her career, Maris has remained focused on her primary role as a Social Worker, offering direct support to youth and families while participating in collaborative efforts to improve local service systems.

Her professional focus has centered on school-linked services, neighborhood resource centers, and preventive interventions for young people. Over the course of her career, she has been employed by both public agencies and nonprofit organizations, while consistently maintaining her primary identity and responsibilities as a front-line Social Worker engaged in direct practice with clients.

Early life and education

Maris was born in Harborside, a medium-sized port city characterized by a mix of residential neighborhoods and industrial zones. She was raised in the North Wharf district, an area marked by varied income levels, heterogeneous cultural and linguistic communities, and ongoing economic transition. Her parents held hourly-wage positions, and the family experienced multiple intra-city moves, reflecting fluctuating housing affordability and employment conditions. As a child and adolescent, she attended North Wharf Primary School, followed by Harborside Central Secondary School.

During secondary school, Maris participated in a peer tutoring initiative and a student-organized food drive, both of which exposed her to structured forms of volunteerism and mutual aid. These early experiences prompted her to consider community service and human services as potential long-term career paths. After completing secondary school, she enrolled at Harborside City College, where she earned an associate degree in human services, receiving foundational preparation in social welfare systems, interviewing skills, and basic case management. She then transferred to the regional State University at Harborside, completing a Bachelor of Social Work (BSW). Continuing her formal education, she obtained a Master of Social Work (MSW) with a concentration in community practice, emphasizing program planning, community organizing, and policy-informed practice.

Early career

Following completion of her MSW, Maris accepted a Social Worker position with the Harborside Department of Youth and Family Services. In this municipal role, she conducted home visits, coordinated closely with school staff, and assisted families in accessing housing assistance, health care, and childcare resources. Her caseload encompassed children with chronic school absenteeism, youth experiencing family conflict, and recently arrived immigrant families adapting to the local educational system.

Maris participated in the department’s pilot program for integrated case management, designed to streamline service access and reduce the number of separate assessments families were required to complete. As a Social Worker in this initiative, she helped design a shared intake form usable across multiple services and collaborated with school counselors, public health nurses, and housing advocates. She also received training in basic conflict resolution and trauma-informed practice and applied these approaches during home visits, family meetings, and school-based conferences.

Community-based practice

After approximately five years with the city department, Maris transitioned to the nonprofit Harborside Neighborhood Resource Network as a Social Worker. This organization operated drop-in centers across several districts, including North Wharf, the neighborhood where she had grown up. At the North Wharf center, Maris organized walk-in hours for youth and families, facilitated small psychoeducational groups, and provided individualized, one-on-one support.

Her responsibilities included assisting youth with major school transitions, such as the move from primary to secondary school and planning for postsecondary education or vocational training. She supported parents in interpreting school policies, navigating special education procedures, and understanding local transportation options that affected school attendance and access to services. Additionally, she coordinated with local libraries and community centers to host information sessions on digital safety, job search strategies, and pathways to public benefits.

School-linked initiatives

Maris later accepted a school-linked Social Worker position that was formally shared between two secondary schools, Harborview Secondary and North Wharf Technical Academy. In this capacity, she divided her time between the two campuses. Her responsibilities included meeting with students referred for social or emotional concerns, conducting basic needs assessments, and linking students and their families to appropriate community resources.

She developed a structured referral pathway that allowed teachers, coaches, and administrative staff to contact her through a secure online form. Upon receiving referrals, Maris scheduled follow-up meetings with students and, when appropriate, with their caregivers. She also coordinated with local mental health clinics to arrange more intensive evaluation and specialized services for students whose needs exceeded the scope of school-based support.

Program development and supervision

Over time, Maris assumed additional responsibilities in program design and staff supervision while continuing to function as a practicing Social Worker. She served as lead Social Worker for a multi-year youth engagement project funded by a regional foundation. The project aimed to improve school attendance and reduce school exclusion through structured mentoring, small group activities, and systematic family outreach.

In her role as lead Social Worker, Maris helped create concise screening tools to identify students who might benefit from early, preventive support. She supervised a small team of junior Social Workers and graduate-level social work interns, providing guidance on documentation standards, confidentiality requirements, and interagency communication protocols. She also coordinated regular case review meetings with school administrators and community partners to monitor progress and adjust interventions.

Professional interests and methods

Maris’s practice as a Social Worker emphasizes accessible services, early intervention, and interprofessional collaboration. She frequently employs strengths-based assessment, solution-focused brief interventions, and structured goal-setting in her work with students and families. When discussing school attendance, substance use risk, or future planning with youth, she incorporates basic motivational interviewing techniques to enhance engagement and support behavior change.

In addition to direct client work, Maris contributes to internal training for new Social Workers within her organization. She has developed orientation materials on mandated reporting requirements, safety planning for home visits, and respectful, culturally responsive communication with families from diverse backgrounds. She has also participated in local interagency committees on youth services, representing the perspective and practice realities of school-linked Social Workers.

Later activities

Maris continues to work as a Social Worker in Harborside, integrating school-based responsibilities with broader community outreach. She maintains a part-time schedule at Harborview Secondary while devoting the remainder of her workweek to the North Wharf neighborhood center. Her ongoing projects include updating the center’s resource directory, piloting a text-message reminder system for appointments, and supporting a youth advisory council that offers feedback on services and suggests improvements.

Throughout her career, Maris has remained focused on her primary role as a Social Worker, providing direct support to youth and families while participating in collaborative efforts to strengthen and improve local service systems.
